title: Phase 12A question-to-evidence relevance and sufficiency authority
problem_statement: Deterministic literal claim support is currently promoted into synthesis without a server-visible original question or complete request scope. FALSE-04 demonstrated that a true quotation about a seven-digit barcode prefix was promoted as an answer to whether an authoritative record binds a complete thirteen-digit barcode to a product.
root_cause: REST and MCP verification accept claims and evidence references but not the original question or an explicit answer-coverage contract. GroundingService infers expected barcode context only from proposed barcode claims; an EXTRACTIVE_STATEMENT can therefore be supported by literal source text without proving entity relevance, request coverage, source authority, or answer sufficiency.

proposed_contract.request_scope: Require bounded original-question text, explicit requested claim keys, and exact subject anchors when the question does not contain a supported exact identifier. The scope is a constraint only, never factual evidence.
proposed_contract.deterministic_constraints: Re-derive recognized exact identifiers and explicit authority, freshness, multi-source, and quotation requirements from the original question; reject missing or conflicting request-scope declarations. Match complete normalized identifier/entity tokens, never prefixes.
proposed_contract.claim_relevance: Every candidate claim must map to a requested answer key and a same-source subject or exact-identifier binding. Exact quotes may enter synthesis only for an explicit quotation request.
proposed_contract.authority_and_time: Required source roles come only from a trusted injected server policy. Missing policy/role or insufficient temporal metadata yields fail-closed abstention.
proposed_contract.sufficiency: All required keys, identifier/entity constraints, authority requirements, freshness requirements, source-count requirements, and contradiction checks must pass before synthesis_claims is nonempty.
proposed_contract.uncertainty: When relevance, authority, temporal validity, or completeness cannot be determined deterministically, return an explicit insufficient assessment and no synthesis claims. No LLM judge or vector similarity acts as factual authority.

threat_model: An LLM proposes a plausible but irrelevant verbatim quote as an answer.
A source discusses a prefix or partial identifier while the question asks about a complete identifier.
A source describes a different product or entity with similar names or overlapping keywords.
The consumer omits requested fields or authority/freshness constraints from its proposed answer scope.
An unauthoritative source is labeled authoritative by caller text or model judgment.
A single exact citation is mistaken for complete, independent, temporally valid support.
A model invents evidence references, source roles, entities, identifiers, or citations.
invariants: Fetched evidence and source metadata remain server-owned; caller prose, claims, scope, authority labels, and citations are proposals only.
Question scope cannot relax any independently detected hard constraint in the original question.
A full identifier must be exactly bound in the source; a numeric prefix or substring is insufficient.
No question-level failure can leave otherwise supported but incomplete claims in synthesis_claims.
Existing supported positive structured-field behavior remains available when complete scope and source binding are proven.
No benchmark-specific task, identifier, domain, answer, threshold, or result is hardcoded.
acceptance_criteria: The baseline reproduces a supported exact quote entering synthesis despite no original-question input.
REST and MCP require the same bounded question-scope contract and expose the same question-level sufficiency assessment.

A prefix-only identifier source, unrelated entity, unrequested quote, missing required field, unknown required source role, stale/unknown temporal record, insufficient-source result, or conflict cannot produce synthesis claims.
A synthetic positive control with an exact identifier/entity, complete required fields, trusted authority role where required, sufficient distinct sources, and current temporal metadata passes.
Citation text integrity, claim-to-source support, question-to-claim relevance, source-authority satisfaction, and full-task acceptance remain separate evidence fields.
Targeted, cumulative, security, real-stack, cross-platform, and exact-SHA CI gates retain their existing thresholds and protections.
negative_paths: Incomplete requested-key coverage, extra claim keys, or non-quotation extractive claims yield no synthesis output.
Prefix-only, wrong-entity, or wrong-product evidence is blocked even when literal text is supported.
Missing/unknown authority roles and unavailable authority policy fail closed.
Missing/out-of-window temporal metadata, insufficient distinct sources, contradictions, and empty evidence fail closed.
Forged or mutated source roles, entity constraints, identifiers, evidence refs, or span refs cannot be accepted.
positive_controls: A fetched record with a complete exact GTIN binding and all requested labeled product fields remains synthesis-safe under a non-authority-required question.
A synthetic trusted source-authority provider plus a complete exact-identifier record passes a question that explicitly requires one of the configured authority roles.
An exact source quotation remains eligible when the original question explicitly requests that quotation and all other scope requirements pass.
observability: Question-level outcome is explicit: sufficient or insufficient.
Reason codes distinguish scope mismatch, unrequested claim, missing identifier/entity binding, missing authority, temporal uncertainty, incomplete coverage, source shortage, and contradiction.
Per-claim support and question-level sufficiency remain separate; sanitized evidence records both without copying secrets or unbounded raw source bodies.
rollback_considerations: No persistent evidence schema or source index mutation is required.
The new request contract changes verification API inputs; rollback requires a new candidate that restores prior input compatibility and removes the new gate coherently.
Do not revert or rewrite Run 003, Run 004, Run 005, or earlier Run 006 evidence.

must_source_edges: REST and MCP pass the original question scope into GroundingService verification.
GroundingService compiles the deterministic question contract before claim promotion.
GroundingService passes question-derived exact identifier constraints into server-owned evidence graph construction.
GroundingService applies question sufficiency after deterministic per-claim verification and before canonical packet emission.
must_document_edges: Only a complete, relevance-aligned, authority/temporal/source-sufficient question assessment may expose claims to synthesis.
Any unresolved question-level requirement returns an empty synthesis claim set and explicit reason codes.
